name: Private Eye Cyclops crossword No 563
preamble: Running clockwise around the shaded squares are the (first and last) names of nine prominent MPs who lost their seats in the 2015 general Election. A thick line separates each entry; no name starts or ends at a corner square. The (52) letters of these names not intersecting with the normal clue answers are: AAAAAAAAA CC DDD EEEEEEEEE HH LLL M NNNNN OOO RRR SSSSS T U VVV W Y

solutions.check: 68 entries verified against the grid image (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping); unclued letters checked against the preamble's list

clue.text: Establishment prodded Boris to accept Tory leader

indicators.note: letters that are prodded get poked out of their places and pushed into a new order
the leader of a word is the letter at its front, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening letter of Tory

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson is nudged into welcoming the head of his own party.
explanation.walkthrough: BORIS accepts T, and the six letters are rearranged into BISTRO. 'Establishment' looks political, but here it means a business premises.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small restaurant, and any shop, bar or eatery can be called an establishment.

clue.text: Sierra Nevada location, one taking Hilary’s lead within a digit

the first letter of Hilary
a toe is a digit of the foot

explanation.surface: A spot in the Sierra Nevada where someone follows Hilary's example, all within a finger or toe.
explanation.walkthrough: A takes H to make AH, which goes inside TOE. Hilary suggests Clinton or Hillary the mountaineer, fitting a mountain range.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Tahoe is a large freshwater lake high in the Sierra Nevada mountains on the California-Nevada border.

clue.text: Result of getting wind of cup size on old movie star (wife leaves)

whatever leaves a word departs from it, so that letter is dropped

Raquel Welch, the 1960s screen star
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.walkthrough: B goes on WELCH, and the W for wife leaves to give ELCH. 'Getting wind' sounds like hearing news, but it means having trapped gas.
explanation.definitionFit: A belch is the burp that comes out when gas builds up in the stomach, i.e. when you have wind.

clue.text: Contemptible Tony agitating with Huw to commandeer Right

taken as written

explanation.surface: Tony Blair stirring things up with Huw Edwards to seize the political right: a contemptible business.

explanation.definitionFit: Someone unworthy deserves no respect, the same as a person held in contempt or scorn.

clue.text: To be a political candidate (a new Democrat), row and hold your ground

blocks.note: in Britain you stand for Parliament
taken as written

a row (rhymes with cow) is a quarrel or fight

explanation.surface: Advice to a fresh Democratic candidate: run for office, have a scrap, and don't back down.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a candidate stands for election rather than runs. Row here is the quarrel, not the boat or the line.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand and fight is to refuse to retreat and face an opponent, which is what holding your ground means.

clue.text: Scandalous secrets that might involve a scrubber

definitions.text: Scandalous secrets that might involve a scrubber

explanation.walkthrough: Scrubber has two senses in Britain: a brush for cleaning and an insulting word for a promiscuous woman. Both fit, one literal and one scandalous.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirty laundry is the idiom for private embarrassing matters, as in 'washing your dirty linen in public'.

clue.text: “Extremely sexy, coming inside undone blouse”, as might be said when you erupt into hanky

definitions.text: as might be said when you erupt into hanky

coming inside means entering, so the pair sits within the other letters
something undone has come apart, so these letters are loosened into a new order

blocks.note: the first and last letters of sexy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A racy compliment about an unbuttoned blouse turns into a polite remark after someone sneezes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an intensifier for 'sexy', but it picks out that word's two ends. 'Erupt into hanky' is a comic way to say sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: English speakers traditionally say these words to someone who has just sneezed into a handkerchief.

clue.text: Take care of Blair – end’s gone quiet

explanation.walkthrough: The Blair here is Cherie, not Tony; she loses her final E before SH is added.
explanation.definitionFit: To cherish someone is to love and protect them, looking after them tenderly.

clue.text: Things from the sewer f*** Sun – let’s split

indicators.note: to split is to break apart, so these letters come apart and regroup

blocks.note: eff is the polite stand-in for the swear word, as in 'eff off'
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude reaction to the Sun newspaper's sewage stories: swear at it and walk out.
explanation.walkthrough: The asterisked word is said aloud as EFF, the usual British euphemism. The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Effluents are liquid wastes discharged from drains, factories and sewage works into rivers or the sea.

clue.text: Oldies might well have been pushed around courtesy of this city official, being sexless

definitions.text: Oldies might well have been pushed around courtesy of this

blocks.note: Bath is a Roman spa city in Somerset, England
a chairman is the official who presides over a meeting

explanation.surface: Pensioners shoved about by a gender-neutral town official.
explanation.walkthrough: The city official is a CHAIRMAN, and taking away the MAN leaves CHAIR, echoing the gender-neutral title. The definition is the long first half.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath chair was a wheeled chair with a hood, used to push invalids and elderly people around spa towns.

clue.text: ‘Grinder’ Maureen: large arse needs reducing by half

taken as written

explanation.surface: A crude jibe at a woman nicknamed Grinder who is told her backside needs to shrink.
explanation.walkthrough: Halving the four letters of the rude word keeps AR. 'Grinder' in quotes looks like a nickname, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Molars are the broad back teeth whose job is to crush and mash food when chewing.

clue.text: I’m surprised it panders to celeb-worshippers

blocks.note: first meaning: a word you exclaim on noticing something unexpected
second meaning: the glossy British celebrity magazine with an exclamation mark in its title

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one sneer at a gossip magazine, but it splits into an exclamation and the magazine's name. Hello! is a British weekly devoted to celebrity photo spreads.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a startled interjection and the title of a famous weekly society magazine.

clue.text: American fighting machine needs new chief

indicators.note: a new chief means a change at the top, so the first letter is swapped for another

blocks.note: a tank is an armoured fighting vehicle

explanation.surface: A US war machine is due a change of commander.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue does not say which letter becomes the new head; the definition and the crossing letters settle on Y. 'American fighting machine' wants to be read together, but American alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Yank is informal, chiefly British slang for a person from the United States, short for Yankee.

clue.text: Quite a goer – day to get over rear screwing

indicators.note: screwing twists something round, so these letters are turned into a new order
getting over something means straddling it, so the outer piece spans the other

blocks.note: Fri is the abbreviation for Friday
taken as written

explanation.surface: A smutty remark about a promiscuous person and a day of bedroom athletics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite a goer' is British slang for someone sexually eager, but here it means a car that goes very fast. The day is FRI, split around the twisted rear.
explanation.definitionFit: A Ferrari is a fast Italian sports car, and a goer is something that moves quickly.

clue.text: Grudge match’s halfway point follows dispatched (again) blokes

indicators.note: the halfway point of a five-letter word is its third, middle letter
to follow is to come after, so this letter goes at the end

blocks.note: sent again, written as re-sent
blokes is British slang for men
the central letter of match

explanation.surface: A tetchy grudge match reaches half-time after some men are sent off again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grudge match' reads as one phrase, but Grudge alone is the definition. Re-sent and resent are spelt the same, which is the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A grudge and resentment are both lasting bitterness felt towards someone over a past wrong.

clue.text: “Mater has not finished, having knocked back a drink” – prince

indicators.note: a word that is not finished stops short of its final letter
to knock something back is to send it backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: mater is Latin, and old public-school slang, for mother: MA
taken as written
a jar is British slang for a drink, especially a pint of beer

explanation.surface: A posh mother is still drinking when the prince arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'going for a jar' means going for a drink, so 'a drink' gives A JAR. Knocked back looks like drinking, but it turns those letters round.
explanation.definitionFit: A maharaja was a great Indian ruler or high prince, the title meaning great king in Sanskrit.

clue.text: Thrusts and withdraws repeatedly? They’re on the receiving end

blocks.note: first meaning: lunges and parries with a sword, the sport of fencing
second meaning: criminals who receive and sell stolen goods

explanation.walkthrough: The first half sounds sexual, in keeping with this puzzle, but it describes swordplay. A fence in criminal slang receives stolen property.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for duelling with foils and a noun for dealers in stolen goods, called receivers.

clue.text: Vatican: so crappy ringing round a province

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A complaint that the Vatican is making a mess while bells ring around a region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Province' can sound ecclesiastical next to the Vatican, but it means a Canadian province. The answer runs across two entries, 38 across and 1 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Nova Scotia is one of the ten provinces of Canada, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Repeat: it’s the end of Dave (Conservative House reduced)

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter, so just that one is kept

blocks.note: the final letter of Dave

explanation.walkthrough: Dave suggests Cameron, the Conservative prime minister, but only his last letter is used. 'Reduced' tells you to abbreviate House.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound repeated back, and to echo is to repeat what someone else has said.

clue.text: One who’d discriminate about just how it was entered in arse?

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the word faces the other way
something entered in is put inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: sic, Latin for 'thus', marks a quotation as copied exactly as it was
an arse is a contemptible person, as is a rat

explanation.surface: A crude question about a bigot and exactly what went where.
explanation.walkthrough: Sic is printed in brackets after a quoted error to show it is reproduced faithfully. Arse is British slang for a fool or a rotter, here RAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A racist is someone who treats people unfairly because of their race, i.e. who discriminates.

clue.text: Cyclops hampered by diabolical time lag designed to stop certain people from drinking in pub?

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is this crossword's setter, so his name stands for I, the way 'me' or 'setter' often does. The definition describes the answer rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: An age limit is the minimum age for something, such as 18 for buying alcohol in a British pub.

clue.text: Waffle and crack that led to Alice’s going down

definitions.text: that led to Alice’s going down

blocks.note: to rabbit, in British slang, is to chatter on at length
a crack is a gap or hole

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit on' is British slang for talking too much, from rhyming slang 'rabbit and pork' for talk. Waffle looks like breakfast but means rambling talk.
explanation.definitionFit: In Lewis Carroll's story Alice follows the White Rabbit and falls down a rabbit-hole into Wonderland.

clue.text: Mucky place, etc. – piss off

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Piss off' reads as a rude dismissal, but off is the instruction to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A cesspit is a pit for sewage and waste, so it is literally and figuratively a dirty place.

clue.text: Bill’s accepting ‘coitus illicitum’ as a science

clue.text: Where to lay your head on the line?

clue.text: Flighty activity of a disgraced Lord at close of play?

clue.text: Improvised missile presently embedded in small testicle

clue.text: Complete show-off of an arse? Just a phase

second meaning: one stage in the monthly cycle of the lunar disc

explanation.walkthrough: 'Just a phase' sounds like excusing teenage behaviour, but it is literal astronomy. Mooning means exposing your bottom as a prank.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a thorough mooning, showing the whole backside, and the phase when the moon appears as a complete disc.

clue.text: Bastard, having finished with clue, flipped

explanation.walkthrough: Arse is British slang for a contemptible person as well as the bottom. The definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Arse over tip is British slang for head over heels, tumbling upside down.
